full_judgment: 48. Upon examination of the allegations and counter-allegations of the parties, it surfaces that the relationship of the parties started to deteriorate when the petitioner-company terminated its agency agreement and thereafter it deteriorated further when the Chairman of the respondent No. 1-company took the issue of termination of agency agreement to the SIAC. Thereafter, the relationship reached its worst level when the Chairman of the respondent No. 1-company abstained from settling the accounts of the respondent No. 1-company, which generated the Writ Petition Nos. 9863 of 2016, 13428 of 2016, 8719 of 2019 and 10645 of 2019. That is to say, because of non-compliance of the Award passed in the Arbitration No. 199 of 2016 by SIAC against the Chairman of the respondent No. 1-company (Mr Sayeed. Hussain Chowdhury), apparently the causes for filing the aforesaid Writ Petitions were created. And, ultimately when the Chairman of the respondent No. 1-company fully ignored his obligation as to complying with the SIAC arbitration award, Execution case being Money Decree Execution Case No. 22 of 2019 has been filed before the learned District Judge Court, Dhaka wherein orders pertaining attachment of scheduled properties, i.e. Bangladesh Shipping Lines Limited, accounts of COSCO Bangladesh etc., are passed. So, it appears to this Court that there truly exists a deadlock situation in the affairs of the respondent No. 1-company.
